newsitem.title: USA: NRC concerned over Northeast Millstone plan.
newsitem.headline: NRC concerned over Northeast Millstone plan.

text.p: The federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) has some doubts that Northeast Utilities is on schedule to get its troubled Millstone nuclear plants back on line, an NRC spokeswoman said on Wednesday

"There's still a whole lot of work to be done," NRC spokeswoman Diane Screnci told Reuters. "They still have a whole lot of milestones to meet, and the ICAVP (Independent Corrective Action Verification Program) is just one step in the process to restart."
Northeast said Tuesday that the ICAVP for Unit 3 was scheduled to begin in May.
Screnci said that the ICAVP, which involves hiring an independent contractor to make sure that Northeast has already spotted any potential problems, was a critical step in the restart process.
"That's something major that they need to accomplish prior to restart. If the contractor finds that they weren't finding problems, that could bring that process to a stop."
Screnci said the NRC had no problem with Northeast making Unit 3 its priority in the restart process.
"We had wanted them to select a unit to be the lead unit, so that we could plan our resources, though had they gone ahead with the other plan, we would have supported that as well."
A Northeast spokesman said Wednesday that the latest meeting with federal regulators was only one step in a long and complex procedure.

"The best way to characterize the meeting is that, this was part of a fairly lengthy process, where we're going to provide a lot of information to the NRC and there's going to be an active exchange between the company and the agency," Northeast spokesman Rich Gallagher told Reuters.

Northeast's modified restart readiness schedule did not change the utility's basic timetable announced last December. Northeast still plans to have one unit ready for restart in the third quarter of this year, one in the fourth quarter, and one in the first quarter of 1998, pending NRC approval.
